schema_history.rdebug-release-gates/2: adds spec_gate mapping, per-gate state, required_execution, blocking, four-state aggregate exit codes and the JSON report. Gate 3 and gate 4 are declared here as NOT_IMPLEMENTED and PROCESS_ONLY so the aggregate can see that they have nothing to run.
schema_history.rdebug-release-gates/3: gate 3 becomes IMPLEMENTED: cold_warm_equivalence now has a command and a verdict. The release runner needs a new runner kind so the gate four-state verdict is consumed rather than collapsed into pass or non-zero, which is what exit_code would do.
schema_history.rdebug-release-gates/4: gate 3 declares the environment it actually needs. It was listed as pure python, which is wrong: it spawns workers that replay, so without the renderdoc module and a capture it aborts as INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE. A pipeline cannot provision what the spec does not declare.
schema_history.rdebug-release-gates/5: gates declare required capabilities as dotted names so the readiness layer can resolve them against a probed environment. This is a declaration only; nothing is provisioned.
schema_history.rdebug-release-gates/6: A gate may declare a lint precondition. Its result is recorded as a lint sub-record on the gate row rather than as a gate of its own, so the gate count and the exit mapping are unchanged.
schema_history.rdebug-release-gates/7: gate 4 becomes IMPLEMENTED: the benchmark archive requirement now has a mechanical decision path. The manifest (docs/validation/benchmark-archive-manifest.json) declares the commit the archived measurements were taken on and the monitored session/latency surface; the gate verifies the archive still covers the code it is attached to, so a monitored change without re-archiving is a REGRESSION and the aggregate can reach PASS only when the archive covers this tree. The gate states its own four-state verdict, consumed as verdict_json, because an exit code cannot tell a stale archive from an unreadable manifest.

note: Gate definitions for DESIGN_SPEC section 4. This file declares what must run before a change can be treated as verified. It is not a pipeline: nothing here schedules, blocks a pull request, or talks to a forge. Running it by hand is still a manual action, and that residual gap is recorded rather than claimed solved.

allowed_skips: Positive control on the state the project is actually in.
Conditional, but not a blanket skip.
Identity is what makes the artefact evidence, so prove it binds.
The real fork is measured, not assumed compliant.
gates.rationale: Stable Core pure logic. No RenderDoc, so it cannot silently skip wholesale; the floor exists to catch a discovery failure that runs nothing.

lint.rationale: Static analysis configured in pyproject.toml with no executor. Four violations survived several full pipelines for that reason.
lint.probe_rationale: A missing ruff launched as `python -m ruff` exits 1, the same code ruff uses for 'found violations'. Without an availability probe an absent tool is reported as a content regression.

gates.rationale: Real replay behaviour. This is the gate that A2-1 applies to: without its environment it skips about 60 of 63 tests, and a bare exit code is not evidence that anything was verified. A missing environment is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
DESIGN_SPEC 2.1 to 2.9 mechanical boundary audit. The script's own exit code and N/N output are the evidence.

DESIGN_SPEC 4.3 cold-equals-warm equivalence. Compares the complete semantic payload of five mandatory cases across four collection points spanning a real worker recycle, and asserts the worker boundary by pid rather than assuming it. No field allowlist and no volatile-field exclusion: a difference is a REGRESSION to be investigated, not tolerated. CAPTURE_PLACEHOLDER is substituted by the runner from the gate spec capture field.

DESIGN_SPEC 4.4 requires session and latency data changes to be archived under docs/validation. The decision path is change coupling: the manifest declares the commit the archived measurements were taken on and the monitored session/latency surface, and the gate verifies the archive still covers the code it is attached to. A monitored change without a new archive is REGRESSION; a missing or unreadable manifest, or an absent declared archive file, is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE -- the same discrimination the fork audit makes between an absent control input and present evidence that disagrees. The D6 benchmark is explicitly not this gate: D6 is performance evidence, not a release gate, and this gate proves coverage, not the absence of regressions.
DESIGN_SPEC 2.1.1. Read-only git inspection of the RenderDoc fork. Consumed as a subprocess exit code; the F1 to F4 logic is never duplicated here.

classification.PASS: checks executed and all of them passed
classification.REGRESSION: checks executed and at least one found a content difference
classification.UNKNOWN: the gate could not form a content conclusion; not a pass, needs a human
classification.INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE: the gate itself could not execute; blocks, and is never reported as a regression
